working_proof.proof: Let C be complete algebraically closed nontrivially real-valued. Let B be a reduced strict affinoid algebra with its faithful spectral norm. Suppose EVERYnonzero spectral norm belongs to |C^x|, and its canonical reduction Btilde=Bcirc/Bcirccirc is an integral domain. Both are explicit hypotheses. Then the spectral norm is MULTIPLICATIVE: normalize any nonzero f,g by scalars of their exact spectral norms; their reductions are nonzero, so their product reduction is nonzero in the domain. Its spectral norm is1, giving ||fg||=||f||||g||. Thus B is a domain and its spectral norm defines an actual analytic point x0 of M(B) with zero kernel.

This point reduces to the generic point of Btilde. Conversely, any analytic point x reducing to that generic point agrees with the spectral norm on EVERYf in B: divide a nonzero f by a scalar c having |c|=||f||. The nonzero reduction of f/c stays nonzero at the generic residue point, hence its evaluated residue is nonzero and |f/c(x)|=1. Therefore x=x0 as an analytic seminorm. This derives uniqueness from norm range and canonical integrality; uniqueness alone is never used to infer equality of whole residue fields.

By the definition of the analytic completed residue field, H(x0) completes honest Frac(B). Its residue field equals Frac(Btilde). For a unit h of H(x0), approximate it by f/g in Frac(B) with error<1, so its norm and residue are preserved. Choose c with |c|=||g||; then g/c is powerbounded of norm1 and f/c is powerbounded because |f/g|<=1. Their canonical residues give the residue of h as (bar f/c)/(bar g/c) in Frac(Btilde). This proves surjectivity; injectivity follows from the generic reduction. The argument uses actual approximation in H(x0), no valuation-defect equality or geometric singleton inference.

An explicit route to the norm-range hypothesis is the complete bounded-normalization/finite-Gauss-norming construction of working254, INCLUDINGits component-dominance addendum. It is UNREVIEWED DATA, not a grant, and must be reconstructed. Its finite injective Tate-polydisc map has Gauss base H(eta), value group exactly |C^x|, and finitely many analytic Gauss-fiber points coming from finite field extensions. A finite valued extension has finite value index: representatives with distinct value classes are linearly independent over the base by unique-minimum valuation. The divisible base group inside the real-valued target then admits no nontrivial finite-index extension. Consequently every Gauss-fiber value lies in |C^x|. The characteristic-polynomial root bound and realization at those finite fibers norm EVERYanalytic function, so every spectral norm belongs to |C^x|. This is the precise finite-fiber hypothesis needed in A1, not a claim that formal flatness alone proves it.
